column1: # The mutants that survive today, per package, as a ratchet.
# package
# Measured 2026-08-16 with gremlins v0.5.0 at --timeout-coefficient 60, and
# re-measured 2026-08-17 under v0.6.0 at the same coefficient. Every count below
# is unchanged across the two, which is the answer to the question a tool bump
# always raises here and the reason none of these numbers moved with it. A count
# here is a promise that this many tests are missing, not a target: every one of
# them is a change to a line that no assertion notices. Lower it as they are
# killed, and never raise it without saying what got worse.
# Three packages, not the tree. These are the ones where a surviving mutant is a
# wrong answer somebody acts on rather than a cosmetic difference: jql builds
# every query and owns the only place a value is quoted, render writes the
# output contract, and site decides what a deployment is and resolves the names
# every command takes. The sweep costs about four minutes on a developer
# machine and considerably more on a runner, which is why it is scheduled.
# `internal/jql` went 16 to 3 on 2026-08-17. Thirteen were killed by assertions
# named in internal/jql/*_test.go; the three below are equivalent mutants, which
# is a different claim from "no test notices" and is why they are written down
# rather than left as a number somebody will try to lower.
#   date.go:367:12   `total > maxDuration-component`, boundary. The two forms
#                    differ only when the sum lands exactly on MaxInt64
#                    nanoseconds. Every unit in dateValueUnits is a whole number
#                    of minutes, so every total is a multiple of 60e9, and
#                    MaxInt64 is odd: the equality is unreachable by
#                    construction rather than untested.
#   token.go:217:10  `start+1 < len(src)`, the guard that reads two runes only
#   token.go:217:13  when two remain. Both mutants make it read one rune past
#                    the end at the end of a query. `src` is one `[]rune(query)`
#                    and every lexer takes it whole with an index, so that rune
#                    is allocator spare and reads as U+0000, which completes no
#                    two-rune operator. The mutants differ from the original
#                    only by an index-out-of-range panic when cap == len, and a
#                    test that arranged that would be asserting Go's size
#                    classes rather than this tokenizer.
# If one of those is ever killed honestly, delete its paragraph and lower the
# count in the same change. The ledger only shrinks.
internal/jql
